## DAR BRONZE PLAQUE Update (Susan)
- Sandy Barry attended the meeting to provide information about the proposed plaque and to field GHC questions
- Julie, Susan, and Sandy met June 10 to discuss "Land Acknowledgment" plaque; wording approved by Cheryll Toney Holley (elected Sonksq/female chief of the Hassanamisco Nipmuc Band), which will be placed somewhere along the Boulevard. The first and last sentences are directly from the Gloucester 400+ land acknowledgement used by the City of Gloucester. The middle sentence was added by Sandy Barry to acknowledge the work of Mary Ellen Lepionka.

*Land Acknowledgment*

The City of Gloucester is located on the traditional and ancestral homeland of the Pawtucket people and their neighbors the Massachusett, Nipmuc, Penacook, and Wampanoag tribes.

They followed the seasons, hunted, fished, raised families, grieved for their dead, nourished their living, shared the stories of their ancestors, and were caretakers of this land.

We recognize and honor the Native and Indigenous peoples who have lived in this territory for more than 10,000 years, are here now, and will be here for generations to come. We acknowledge our responsibility to include Native people and perspectives in our efforts to share Gloucester's history, including the painful history of their genocide and forced removal from this territory.

MARKER PLACED BY CAPE ANN CHAPTER
NATIONAL SOCIETY DAUGHTERS OF THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION

- Bob made a motion to approve the plaque, Maggie seconded, all in favor

## CPC UPDATE (Susan/Maggie)

The following 3 meet the CPA designations for historically significant (have 1+ of the 5 designations)

### 6 GHC VOTES FOR BELOW:
- **GLO.1337 North Shore Arts: rehab work**
  *Statement of Historic Significance*
  11 Pirates Lane is significant as a rare surviving waterfront industrial building that was adaptively reused in 1922 as the permanent home of the North Shore Arts Association. The property embodies Gloucester's transition from a maritime fishing economy to an internationally recognized center for American art. For over a century it has served as a focal point for the Cape Ann art colony, preserving both the city's maritime heritage and its nationally important artistic legacy.
  Bob made a motion, Maggie seconded, all in favor

- **GLO.199 Giles Chapel/Rocky Neck Cultural Ctr: front door protection, floors**
  *Statement of Historic Significance*
  The former Giles Chapel was constructed in 1877 by prominent local businessman Augustus Wonson for the Baptist Church and Sabbath School serving Rocky Neck. He named it in memory of his deceased sister, Lydia Giles, and her husband. At the time, Rocky Neck's post–Civil War population had grown enough to support both its own school and neighborhood chapel, reflecting the area's emergence as a distinct village within Gloucester. The former chapel is significant because it embodies several important themes in Gloucester's history: the development of Rocky Neck as a fishing village, nineteenth-century religious and community life, the philanthropy of the Wonson family, Carpenter Gothic architecture, and the successful preservation and adaptive reuse of a historic building that continues to serve the public as a cultural center.
  Bob made a motion, Ralph seconded, all in favor

- **GLO.1420 Gloucester Stage: Phase 2 of brickwork**
  *Statement of Historical Significance*
  The Gloucester Stage/Twin Lights Garage building, built in 1915, is historically significant because it:
  - Represents Gloucester's transition from the bicycle era to the automobile age and the rise of tourism on Cape Ann.
  - Is an intact example of an early twentieth-century purpose-built commercial garage designed by local architect Ezra Phillips.
  - Is associated with nationally important artist Stuart Davis, who immortalized the building in several paintings.
  - Illustrates the adaptive reuse of a historic industrial building into a major regional cultural institution.
  - Continues to serve as a prominent landmark at the entrance to East Gloucester's historic waterfront and Rocky Neck Cultural District.
  Bob made a motion, Maggie seconded, all in favor

- **GLO.1055 Davis-Freeman House/Wellspring - siding repair and replacement, restoration of period trim and decorative features, and rot repair**
  *Statement of Historic Significance*
  The c.1709 Davis-Freeman House is one of the oldest and most architecturally significant properties in Gloucester. Equally important is the human history this house represents. The Freeman family, descended from Robin Freeman, a man who purchased his own freedom in Gloucester in 1769, owned and called this property home for over 100 years, from 1826 until 1931. Wellspring House has done remarkable work uncovering and sharing this once-untold story through the "History Lives Here" exhibit. The Davis-Freeman House is historically significant not only as one of Gloucester's oldest surviving homes and an outstanding example of early colonial construction, but also as a rare place where architectural history, early community development, transportation history, and African American heritage intersect. Its preservation allows visitors to understand more than three centuries of Gloucester's evolving social and cultural history.
  Bob made a motion, Ralph seconded, all in favor

- **GLO.BG Manship: barn restored – REQUESTED GHC LETTER 6/11/25**
  The Manship estate is historically significant because it:
  - is the home and studio of internationally renowned sculptor Paul Manship;
  - preserves an exceptionally intact early-20th-century artist's compound integrated with Gloucester's granite quarry landscape;
  - represents Cape Ann's nationally important artistic community;
  - documents three generations of working sculptors; and
  - continues to serve as a living center for artistic creation, fulfilling its historic function while preserving an important piece of American cultural heritage.
  Bob made a motion, Ralph seconded, all in favor

- **UU Cemetery: Phase 2, structural engineer for tombs; GHC LETTER WRITTEN APRIL 2, 2025**
  *Statement of Historic Significance*
  The Unitarian Universalist (formerly Universalist) Cemetery on Church Street in Gloucester is historically significant because it preserves the physical and cultural legacy of the first Universalist congregation in the United States, founded in 1779 by John Murray. Together with the adjacent meetinghouse, the cemetery forms one of the country's most intact surviving Universalist religious landscapes.
  Bob made a motion, Tim seconded, all in favor

## REGISTER OF HISTORIC BUILDINGS
- Central database for the city of all historic buildings
- Subcommittee proposal: Susan, Ralph, Julie
- 1900 and 1920 year of build was arbitrarily assigned, these need to be corrected
- Start with determining actual build year of 3,200 houses listed as 1900

  - Stephanie Buck working on a small list located in or near Eastern Point built 1900 per city
- Benefit, corrected for: Demo-delay list; Tax assessment records; MACRIS
- CORRECTIONS TO CITY YEAR OF BUILD: inform Tim Good of changes

## CONSIDERATION OF A LANESVILLE/Lane's Cove NATIONAL REGISTRY DISTRICT APPLICATION (Ralph)
- June 24 meeting to discuss: Ralph, Susan, Wendy Frontiero
- Based on MACRIS GLO.K LANESVILLE CENTER, October 2016, by Wendy Frontiero + K Boomer, and based on Russell and Melissa Hobbs' Lanesville buildings research, and additional research and photos would be needed
- Several years ago, an attempt was made to designate Lanesville center as part of the National Register; met with critiques from village residents about restrictions and tourism
- Ralph explains that they are zeroing in on a smaller area of Lanesville center, which includes Lane's Cove, the Fish Shack, cemetery and a few smaller buildings surrounding that area that are publicly owned, or privately owned that Ralph will speak with directly.
  - The fish shacks, seawall, and cemetery would qualify for grants to fix them up if the National Register designation was passed.
- If successful, the hope is to expand the area over time once more people from Lanesville are on board.
- Wendy assumes that $20,000 would be necessary for her work, which could possibly come from CPC funding for next year. Maggie will look into whether this research qualify for CPC funding.

**CALENDAR: Thursday July 16, ZOOM, 7:00 pm, Wendy Frontiero; topic: Gorton's Legacy**
Registration: https://jonathanbayliss.org/event-6397589
Newburyport Model Ship Show: July 25 - August 1, 2026; Ralph has two ships in the show

headline: Commission elected officers, approved DAR plaque wording, a new house plaque, and voted historic significance for six CPC-funded projects.
summary: The Gloucester Historical Commission elected new officers, approved wording for a DAR Land Acknowledgment plaque and a new historic house plaque at 1245 Washington St, and voted historic significance for six CPC-funded preservation projects (North Shore Arts, Giles Chapel/Rocky Neck Cultural Ctr, Gloucester Stage, Davis-Freeman House/Wellspring, Manship estate, and UU Cemetery). The meeting also covered updates on demolition delay, MACRIS listings, tercentenary markers, a Register of Historic Buildings project, and a possible Lanesville/Lane's Cove National Register district application.
decisions: Elected GHC officers: Julie as Secretary, Maggie Debbie as Vice-chair, and Susan as Chair; all in favor.
Approved the wording of the DAR Bronze Plaque (Land Acknowledgment); all in favor.
Accepted the wording of the historic house plaque for 1245 Washington St, Lanesville; all in favor.
Voted historic significance for GLO.1337 North Shore Arts (rehab work); all in favor.
Voted historic significance for GLO.199 Giles Chapel/Rocky Neck Cultural Ctr (front door protection, floors); all in favor.
Voted historic significance for GLO.1420 Gloucester Stage (Phase 2 of brickwork); all in favor.
Voted historic significance for GLO.1055 Davis-Freeman House/Wellspring (siding repair, trim restoration, rot repair); all in favor.
Voted historic significance for GLO.BG Manship (barn restored); all in favor.
Voted historic significance for UU Cemetery (Phase 2, structural engineer for tombs); all in favor.
